title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Beta SDKs for the 2026-07-28 stateless-MCP spec are here — all four Tier 1 SDKs testable now
bullets.summary: You can now validate the forthcoming stateless core, Extensions, Tasks, MCP Apps, and OAuth/OIDC-aligned auth against real workloads: Python v2 and TypeScript v2 (new package names, so installing them is the opt-in) plus Go and C# betas (Go/C# streamable-HTTP accepts 2026-07-28 only with Stateless=true). Final spec ships Jul 28; the ten-week window is for testing before then.
bullets.how: Yesterday's item was the RC announcement; this is the actionable follow-through. We now have a concrete way to test each Construct MCP server against the breaking changes before Jul 28 rather than waiting for GA. Stand up a beta-SDK harness this week, run the fleet through it, and fix anything that breaks under stateless before the deadline goes hard.

bullets.title: Pipedrive ships a native MCP server — CRM data becomes agent-callable with permissions + audit trail
bullets.summary: Pipedrive's native MCP server lets ChatGPT, Claude, and other MCP clients read and act on live CRM data in real time while respecting existing user permissions and keeping a full audit trail of every action.
bullets.how: The CRM layer graduating to MCP is exactly the plumbing PRAGMA's operator wedge needs: one Construct agent that reads pipeline state and takes governed, audited actions. Not our current CRM, but the pattern — vertical SaaS exposing permissioned, audited MCP surfaces — is the one to wrap behind Pulse rather than hand-rolling integrations.

bullets.title: AVCLabs launches an MCP server bringing AI video enhancement + image segmentation into agent workflows
bullets.summary: Upscaling, enhancement, and precise image segmentation (cutouts/masking) are now callable as MCP tools inside an agent pipeline rather than manual desktop steps.
bullets.how: Maps to Brand 9 Signs creative production: an agent that segments a subject, cleans a plate, and upscales assets for large-format signage without a human in the editor. Bank it alongside Omneky as a candidate vertical-creative MCP behind Pulse; test output quality at signage resolution before committing.

bullets.title: Agent-startup funding keeps flowing but tilts to infrastructure — LinqAlpha leads early July with a $22M Series A
bullets.summary: Early July logged ~$37M across three disclosed agent rounds (LinqAlpha $22M Series A in front), trailing late June's heavier prints (8090 $135M, Trase $107M, Sail Research $80M), with the week's dollars concentrating in AI infrastructure over application agents.
bullets.how: Market signal, not a tool: capital is rewarding the infra/harness layer (where our durable edge sits) while the 'two people can ship a real agent product' dynamic keeps commoditizing single-purpose app agents. Reinforces staying in owned orchestration + memory rather than competing as one more vertical agent.

bullets.title: arXiv: Bridging Requirements and Architecture — Multi-Agent Orchestration with External Knowledge and Hierarchical Memory
bullets.summary: Proposes a planner/executor/reviewer orchestration that grounds agents in external knowledge and a hierarchical memory, with explicit protocols for cache-sharing and consistency so shared context stays coherent and critics check claims against tool outputs.
bullets.how: Direct map to The Construct's harness: ~/.hermes/memories/ (hierarchical memory), CLAUDE.md locked rules (external knowledge/spec), and our verification steps (the reviewer/critic role). Use the cache-sharing + consistency framing to tighten how agents share memory without contaminating each other, and treat the reviewer role as a first-class step.

praxis_lesson: On a slow Sunday the signal is continuity, not novelty — the MCP substrate keeps hardening (beta SDKs now let us test the stateless fleet before Jul 28) and the CRM/creative layers keep exposing permissioned, audited MCP surfaces (Pipedrive, AVCLabs). The move is unchanged and now overdue for execution: run every Construct server through the beta-SDK harness this week so nothing goes dark on Jul 28, wrap vertical MCPs (CRM, creative) behind Pulse instead of hand-building integrations, and keep the durable edge in the harness — hierarchical memory, owned orchestration, and a real reviewer/verification step — as base models and app agents commoditize.
